statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so there is no current price path to score. Friday's inside-range two-way session, a VIX of 14.87 and a 10-year that retraced off a 19-year intraday high keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. One window is flagged: the Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where an unpriced weekend set - a rejected Hormuz reopening plan, a widened financial-isolation campaign and intercepted Houthi launches at Saudi targets - meets the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; a 19-year-high yield that closed off its extreme and an open diplomatic channel frame the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is still Friday's session: front NQ futures settled at 30,889.25, up 0.40%, inside a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range, while the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 13.38-35.30 52-week range. Current reporting describes the Nasdaq as roughly 3.2% higher on the week and a fresh record weekly close, with confluent resistance noted near 30,762.

The informative evidence sits in the driver assets rather than in equities. The 10-year Treasury yield traded to 5.233% intraday on Friday, reported as its highest level since 2007, and then closed back near 5.167% inside a 5.153-5.233% day range. A driver asset that prints a 19-year extreme and retracts from it is mean reversion functioning, not failing, and that materially constrains the case for a pathological equity path. The latest H.15 release, for 24 September, shows the 2-year at 4.87%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.88%. Current market pricing places the odds of a further quarter-point increase at the October meeting above 70%.

Energy eased into the weekend. WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33% on the day and about 7.4% on the week, and Brent at $104.32, down 2.14%, after Iran called on the United States to return to an interim peace deal. Both remain sharply higher on the month, Brent by about 20%, and the national average gasoline price of $4.49 compares with $4.10 a month earlier, so the inflation channel that has been driving the long end is intact even after a softer week.

The weekend geopolitical set is unresolved rather than escalating. President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on 26 September; on 27 September Iran's foreign minister said Tehran had seen the reported remarks but still awaited an official response through mediators, and described diplomacy as the only route out of the conflict. Treasury measures targeting Iran's aviation sector were announced alongside flight restrictions by the UAE, Turkey and Oman, Saudi Arabia called for UN backing for freedom of navigation, Saudi air defences intercepted two drones and a ballistic missile on 26 September, and Israel struck a Hezbollah weapons facility in southern Lebanon the same day. Commercial traffic through the strait is reported roughly 75% below pre-conflict levels. Separately, current reporting cites an expectation that US strikes on Iran would resume only after the November midterm elections, which defers rather than removes the acute discontinuity risk.

Tail therefore stays at 6. With no venue open there is no observable persistent one-way structure, no shallow-pullback sequence, no failed retracement and no session-extreme holding, and the one driver asset that did reach an extreme retraced from it. Stress remains elevated at 57 on the long-end level, above-70% October hike pricing, a 20% monthly Brent gain, the unresolved chokepoint and a macro week that front-loads Core PCE on 30 September, ISM Manufacturing on 1 October and payrolls on 2 October into consecutive sessions. Confidence of 68 reflects current verified levels, yields, energy, volatility and calendar against a price path that is now more than 34 hours stale. One window is flagged: the Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where an unpriced weekend set meets the thinnest liquidity of the week. The shared Finviz context file was read and found stale and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was not used as evidence in this assessment.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 07:00Z on Saturday 26 September to 06:00Z on Sunday 27 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Every hour carries a published Claude assessment. Tail eased from 8 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 47 to 57 on the rate and Gulf backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 84 down to 69 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the sixteenth slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours, ramps back through 12 as the reopen approaches, peaks at 18 in the reopen hour itself, then eases through 15, 13, 12, 11, 10 and 9 as live discovery resumes. Stress runs between 55 and 61 on a 10-year that printed 5.233% before closing near 5.167%, a 30-year at 5.47%, above-70% odds of an October Fed hike, Brent about 20% higher on the month, a rejected seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, a widened financial-isolation campaign and intercepted Houthi launches at Saudi targets. Confidence bottoms at 62 in the last closed hours before recovering to 76 once roughly a full overnight session of live tape exists. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the only flagged window is the 22:00Z-23:59Z reopen.
